definitions.explanation: In geometry, the portion of a line between two endpoints. Unlike a line, which extends infinitely in both directions, a line segment has a definite length.

examples.japanese: {線分|せんぶん}ABの{長|なが}さを{求|もと}めなさい。
examples.english: Find the length of line segment AB.

examples.japanese: {二点|にてん}を{結|むす}ぶ{線分|せんぶん}を{引|ひ}いた。
examples.english: I drew a line segment connecting two points.

examples.japanese: {三角形|さんかっけい}の{各辺|かくへん}は{線分|せんぶん}であり、その{長|なが}さの{合計|ごうけい}が{周|しゅう}の{長|なが}さになる。
examples.english: Each side of a triangle is a line segment, and the sum of their lengths is the perimeter.

notes:
Composed of {線|せん} (line) and {分|ぶん} (part, segment). A fundamental geometry term taught in elementary and middle school mathematics. The concept distinguishes a bounded portion of a line (with two endpoints) from a full {直線|ちょくせん} (line, extending infinitely) or a {半直線|はんちょくせん} (ray, extending infinitely in one direction).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {線分|せんぶん}の{長|なが}さ: length of a line segment
- {線分|せんぶん}の{中点|ちゅうてん}: midpoint of a line segment
- {線分|せんぶん}を{引|ひ}く: to draw a line segment
- {線分|せんぶん}ABを{二等分|にとうぶん}する: to bisect line segment AB

RELATED TERMS:
- {直線|ちょくせん}: straight line — extends infinitely in both directions
- {半直線|はんちょくせん}: ray — has one endpoint, extends infinitely in one direction
- {辺|へん}: side (of a polygon) — a line segment forming part of a shape
